name: frisbii-transform-mcp

tools.name: search_endpoints
tools.description: Search the live OpenAPI specification of the Frisbii Transform (Billwerk+ Transform) REST API. Returns matching endpoints as 'METHOD /path — summary' lines. Call without a query to get an overview. Use describe_endpoint for parameter and schema details.

query.description: Search terms matched against path, summary, operationId and tags (all terms must match)

tools.name: describe_endpoint
tools.description: Get details for one endpoint from the live OpenAPI spec: path/query parameters and request body schema (required properties are marked with *). Response schemas are omitted by default to keep the answer small — request them via include_response_schemas only when you need to know the response shape in advance. List endpoints support pagination via 'take' and cursor-based 'from' query parameters.

path.description: Endpoint path as returned by search_endpoints, e.g. /api/v1/customers/{id}

include_response_schemas.description: Also include full response schemas (default false; makes the output much larger)

tools.name: call_endpoint
tools.description: Execute an authenticated request against the Frisbii Transform REST API (sandbox environment: https://sandbox.billwerk.com). Use describe_endpoint first to learn required parameters and body shape. Returns the HTTP status and the JSON response body; API error responses are passed through so they can be corrected. PERFORMANCE: for list endpoints always pass 'fields' to project the response down to the properties you actually need — full entities are very large. Entity Ids are MongoDB ObjectIds: the first 8 hex chars encode the creation time as Unix seconds in hex. For time-window queries on list endpoints, try seeding the cursor query parameter 'from' with a synthetic id, e.g. hex(unixSeconds) + '0000000000000000', to start listing near that point in time instead of paginating from the beginning (verify the first page and fall back to normal pagination if the API rejects it).

path.description: Endpoint path, e.g. /api/v1/customers/{id}. Placeholders are filled from pathParams.

pathParams.description: Values for {placeholders} in the path, e.g. {"id": "5f6b…"}

fields.description: Project the JSON response down to these properties (dot paths, applied to each array item), e.g. ["Id", "StartDate", "Customer.Name"]. Strongly recommended for list endpoints.

tools.name: read_docs
tools.description: Read the official Frisbii Transform documentation (guides and concepts: webhooks, dunning, billing flows, self-service portal, SubscriptionJS, changelog). Call without arguments to get the index of all pages, then call again with a page path to read one. Use the OpenAPI tools (search/describe/call_endpoint) for concrete API calls; use this for conceptual questions the spec does not answer.

page.description: Page path from the index, e.g. /docs/webhooks.md — omit to get the index

tools.name: refresh_spec
tools.description: Force a reload of the Frisbii Transform OpenAPI specification from the server. Normally not needed — the spec is cached for one hour and fetched automatically.

instructions:
Frisbii Transform (Billwerk+) REST API, sandbox environment. All endpoints come from the live OpenAPI spec.
Workflow: search_endpoints -> call_endpoint. Use describe_endpoint only when the parameter overview from search is not enough (e.g. to see a request body schema).
On list endpoints ALWAYS pass 'fields' to call_endpoint to project the response; full entities are very large. Paginate with take (max 500) and the cursor query param 'from'.
Entity ids are Mongo ObjectIds; the first 8 hex chars encode the creation time (unix seconds, hex). For time-window list queries, try seeding 'from' with hex(unixSeconds) + '0000000000000000' and verify the first page; fall back to normal pagination if rejected.
For conceptual questions (webhooks, dunning, billing flows) use read_docs, not the API spec.
